questions: Does the eyelid drooping improve after rest or sleep?
Does the drooping tend to worsen later in the day?
Does the double vision or eyelid drooping fluctuate during the day?
Do you have difficulty chewing, swallowing, or keeping food or liquids from going down the wrong way?
Does your speech become slurred or softer when you talk for a while?
Do you develop facial weakness or difficulty smiling after prolonged activity?
Do your neck, arm, or leg muscles become weak with use and improve with rest?
Have you had any shortness of breath, especially when lying down or after exertion?
Did the eyelid drooping begin suddenly?
Is the drooping present in both eyes?
Do you have severe headache or pain around the affected eye?
Is the pupil of the affected eye noticeably larger or smaller than the other pupil?
Have you had any recent injury, surgery, or infection involving your head, neck, or eye?
Do you have a history of thyroid disease or another autoimmune disease?
Are you taking any medicines known to cause muscle weakness or eyelid drooping?
